I purchased this game without knowing anything about it. It was on a 80% off sale s
it piqued my interest and as several of my friends had it I gave it a shot. I give this
game a 10/10 for its design, polish and addictive gameplay and would dare to say its
worth even full prize.
CONTENT
I spent several hours already and even tho its always the same (protect your orb and
kill off any critters before they can reach you) theres a ton of diversity in form of
gems, skills, map types, special challenges, tasks etc etc. I didnt yet uncover the
whole map or unlock every skill or tower or gem but so far I m busy whenever I find
the time to log in. It shows that this game isnt "new" as it got additional content
en masse over time and being faced with all of it now is kinda overwhelming but also
very exciting as I realize I ll play this for a looooooooooong time.
THE GOAL
You ll be thrown into a maze with 1 orb at the end and 1 or multiple entries for
critters. Sometimes the map also has Monster spawners in them including even more
critters per wave. Each map has a pre-defined number of waves coming at you and
also pre-determined critter strenghts. Each passing second will contribute you with
mana, killing a critter adds yet more mana and of course there are other means to
tap mana (environmental, gems, shrines). You use that mana in order to build stuff,
create gems or upgrade existing gems. You can also just let it collect which enables
you to increase your "mana level" representing your "interest" known from other games.
Basically the more interest you can accumulate the higher the bonuses you ll get so
the game "taunts" you with trying to beat the map with the least necessary tools
forcing you to keep trying new combinations in order to maximize your result.
TOWERS
I call em towers but in reality these only represent the bases of your mazes (hey,
that rhymed). Things like a tower foundation or trap foundation or booster
foundations. All of these dont do anything on their own but require gems placed into
them in order to damage critters.
GEMS
There is a whole list of different gems with different attributes. Some damage, others
debuff or buff. You dont have access to all of them at all times. The map you play
decides which gem types are available to you. Gems can be placed or upgraded as PURE
which means their attribute is especially strong or you can combine different colors
of gems in order to combine their attributes. This means that both attributes become
weaker then in a pure gem but the obvious advantage is that you now use 2 attributes
at the same time. You can combine as many as 4 different colors in a single gem.
Using multi-colored gems will increase their upgrade cost as well. Theres a whole
segment of theory crafting behind the combination of gems. I didnt get all of it yet
but I realize it supports rather INSANE combos which enables you to push  your results
into incredible heights.
SKILLS and TALISMANS
These represent a kind of progression curve for you. Skill points are mostly dependant
on your level (each level grants you a certain number of points and also certain feats
and tasks in the game do the same) and let you "purchase" bonuses in certain areas.
Maybe you d like to get more mana per kill or make certain types of gems stronger?
There are 25 skills to chose from and each one can be upgraded "unknown" times (my
highest so far is 15 and I dont think it ends there anytime soon). In addition unspent
skill points increase your starting mana so again you are faced with hard decisions as
being able to create and place strong gems before the first wave appears can represent
easy-mode. You can reset your skills and redistribute your skills at any time allowing
you to micro-manage for specific maps.
Talismans on the other hand are fueled by shadow cores and these are aquired by
defeating enemies in general and certain critter types. Before you can use shadow cores
you gonna need talismans and getting them is kind of a lottery thing. Theres a whole
list of different types at different rarities. You have a "wheel" of amulettes enabling
you to place a finite amount of them so replacing or keeping them in stock is a good
idea later on once you start to "optimize" your amulets for the maps you run. The ones
I used so far only have minor bonuses (up to +9% on certain things) but I havent found
any higher rarity ones yet. You can use your shadow cores to boost the rarity chance of
any talismans as well.
MAPS
Maps are unique in design and each one of them has a specific list of gems it allows to
use. That doesnt mean you have access to all of them at the start as certain gem types
need to be unlocked first before you can use them."Mazing" is a critical thing inside
maps which you accomplish by placing walls in a pattern to force critters to take a
longer route or come by certain spots multiple times in order to increase your possible
kill time or make your placed gems more valuable (by being able to attack passing matters
more then once with the same gem). Many maps also have structures or other specials
which represent additional challenges. This could be mana wells, monster dens, shrines,
spectres and (probably) many more (those are the only ones I had so far).
ENDGAME
I m still busy unlocking stuff so probably havent seen half of everything but I spotted
the "Endurance mode" already which is activatable whenever you beat a map and represents
"open mode". Probably not "open" as they have a finite number of waves but the ones I
sampled so far ramp up so quickly in difficulty that I gonna need a lot more levels,
skills and resources in general to get em done. I read that some of them require
"multiple hours" to complete so looking forward to the fun. At the moment my wizard is
to weak and cannot beat more then a couple waves in endurance mode before he gets overrun.
There are not really any "hard limits" on stuff like in other TD games where you can upgrade
your towers a finite number of times before you reach the "max". I ve seen videos with
incredible gem levels, wizard levels and overall numbers shown on the screen rivaling a T13
rift run in Diablo3 (sorry). None of these can be reached with simply beating a map. You
gonna need certain wizard levels, certain skill levels, certaon talisman set-ups and
certain gem combinations in order to unlock them. Its the carrot which pushes you even
further. I know I ll be there eventually myself but first I need to unlock all the required
skills, farm more shadow cores, get more skill points etc etc in order to be prepared.
You dont start a new map completely at zero. All the shadow cores, skill points, skills
and talismans you aquire beforehand are at your disposal and stay with you in between
maps making your wizard stronger the longer and more you play. I love this "nurturing"
of a character of mine and seeing myself become stronger over time
Another strong point for the game is that unlike other TD games you can use multiple
strategies to beat a map. There are certain set-ups which allow you optimal results and
these get fine-tuned all the time by hard-core players going after the elusive high-score
(each map saves your highest score as a taunt for you to beat) but you have a lot more leeway
to beat maps "regulary" giving you a lot of freedom and choice.
UNKNOWN STUFF
I stumbled across things like a "compass" which I can manipulate but dont have a clue what
to do with yet. Combining stuff also is obvious at first but there are detals to it that
will be hidden to you until you start to experiment around. I havent seen half the maps yet
but many hold extra challenges which force you to think about what you do and WHEN to do it.
The game seems to evolve constantly and doesnt remain static. It fascinates me and hours keep
going by at an alarming rate.
I dont regret buying this game and recommend it 100%

This is one of those games I find it hard to recommend to many people. However for a Tower Defense game, GemCraft - Chasing Shadows is pretty great.
I won't be discussing the plot of the series, but I will say there are four games in the series so far. The first three being flash games: Chapter One: The Forgotten, Chapter Zero: The Gem of Eternity, Lost Chapter: Labyrinth, and finally Chapter 2: Chasing Shadows.
The gameplay is very much of what you expect of a Tower Defense game. Place some towers, set up defenses, and don't let the monsters get to your base. However it isn't bright and colorful in this world. Everything is grim, dark, and depressing. After all, the world is much of a wasteland with those monsters around.
Your main line of defense is gems. Yes, gems. These are your "defense units" of the game. There are a total of 9 colors of gems in the game, each with their unqiue own effects (note that Lime from Labyrinth is removed and White and Black are added).
Besides being able to build towers, you are able to build walls, amplifiers (which are towers that power other towers..but they need a gem equipped to be used), and traps (which focus on effects more than damage).
..I'd go on to cover the rest of the gameplay, but I'd run out of space by the time I do so. Plus there's an in-game tutorial feature that helps you learn over time about almost everything gameplay wise.
The presentation as I said before is dark and depressing. However I did not mention how..enchanting the music is. It's hard to explain, but there's just something about the soundtrack that I really enjoy. While we're talking about presentation, the game obviously looks better than the first three games due to it not being limited as a flash game this time around. Heck, I can say it runs better as well.
Overall, I do enjoy GemCraft - Chasing Shadows. Now there's one thing I lacked to mention. The game is
grind heavy. You'll end up grinding and backtracking to various levels to level up, just to be able to take on new levels, or possibly just to unlock something you missed before such as a Skill Tome or Battle Trait. There is also the overabundance of achievements, 419 to be specific. Most of which are simple, but eventually it will be difficult or possibly time wasting. There is also the "Iron Wizard" mode that can be unlocked. Meaning, you guessed it, this grind heavy game just got harder. Also there's a single achievement tied to it. "Good luck."
If you're a "Completionist" or happen to be a casual player, you're better off turning back now as this is a long game. A
long game. However if you're looking for something to spend your time on, and don't mind the repetitive grinding, I may as well recommend this game to ya. The full price of $9.99 isn't that bad, especially looking at how much playtime you get off of it.

As someone who's played all previous games in the series, I had high hopes for Chasing Shadows. The flash version blew those expectations out of the water, and the Steam version has only improved this game. I'd consider this game to be the best tower defense game out there.
Pros:
- Custom window size
- Easy to pick up
- Tons of replayability (endurance mode)
- Lots of achievements
- Battle traits don't cost any shadow cores (compared to the flash version)
- Fun to play and always engaging
- More fields (compared to the flash version)
- Customization options to suit your playstyle
Cons:
- This game is normally 10 dollars, which might be overpriced for some (I got mine on a sale)
- Advanced mana-farms/endurance mode play can lag low-end computers
- Story isn't very strong (but you don't play tower defense games for the story)
If I had to rate it, I would give it a 9.5/10. This game is a must-have for any tower defense enthusiasts, and even if you don't play tower defense, I highly recommend you give it a try :)

Loving the game thus far. If you’re on the fence for this game but have a strong fondness for Action games and/or JRPS with great, unique stories, I’d say the game is worth it during the current sale. However, just know that this is a (still) an unoptimized PC port before you buy it. If you’re like me and have AMD, here are my recommendations:
1) If you encounter the white screen of the death, click here. This fixed the issue for me. Essentially, I was running on the most recent AMD driver, but the game files (as the time of this writing) was not able to recognize the latest version of my driver. Basically, I had to download an older AMD driver for the game to recognize my graphics card.
2) To optimize performance and stabilize fps, download the FAR mod (which is a google search away). Hopefully this will help improve performance, as this mod did for me.
For reference, here are my specs:
Intel Core i5 6500
AMD R9 380 4GB
8 GB of RAM
If you have specs similar or greater than mine, I think you’re in good shape to have 1080p 60 fps for the most part (but I’m still a PC newbie, so sorry I mess anything up :/ ).
For the review bit:
It takes some patience to get the port running decently, but once you do, the game really takes you on a ride, at least based on the 8-9 hours I played so far. Highlights include:
-	Fluid combat system, but takes a while to get used to
-       God-tier soundtrack, and might be the best of 2017 so far
-	Fantastic art direction and character design
-	LOADS of side quests and content to discover
-	Fishing (?)
-	Great story and unique premise
-	Interesting mix of Platinum Games combat and some Dark Souls aspects sprinkled in here and there (makes more sense once you play it)
-	2Booty
Obviously, as with all other games, Nier: Automata may not be for everyone. But like I said, if you fancy Action games and/or JRPS with great, unique stories, you can’t go wrong for this game.
Note to Square-Enix: try not to rush your PC ports next time. I noticed that Nier wasn’t your only game to encounter some major PC drawbacks, especially in the cases of Just Cause 3 and Deus Ex: Mankind Divided. It’s clear that your company publishes good games, but major performance issues and the following negative word of mouth has alienated some eager consumers from purchasing more of your products, me included. Just a pro-tip

This game has almost everything going for it.. great graphics, good story, good voice acting, and even though it's meant for controller, the gameplay is still palatable via the keyboard/mouse control scheme.  Despite this you need to be aware that it is an unforgiving "START OVER IF YOU DIE" based game.  What makes this worse, is you have to find out how to save, sometime later, after a major boss battle.  No auto-checkpoints here.
If you are one of the mega-god gamers that never die in a game, great, this review isn't for you--move along.  To those others who do not find the no save/no checkpoint type of game easy... Is it worth it to persevere, get better and get to the end?  Yes.  However, the beginning experience of the game may also make you want to get a refund (many in the community forums have indicated they've done so).
Next, getting out of the game (or rather back to the main menu) can't be done during combat segments in the early part of the game where you don't have a menu.  So if you're still stuck in the repeat ad nauseum hell of a beginning, don't try letting yourself die--you'll have too much auto-heal power, that will take you to the end of the opening segment, so best just ALT-F4.
While someone may have thought that "saving" could be part of the story, that person was a moron.  If you consider the "auto-healing" mechanic they've added, and that we're dealing with bots, I'd expect the standard checkpoint system in most of these console conversion games to be more on par with the story than a manual save.  This design is an obvious time-gating mechanism to allow them to increase the average playthrough time against a short story.  Mr. Developer, I see through the thinly veiled attempt, and am not amused.
Finally, there are some wierd glitches, and strange camera behavior during boss battles.  It's very easy to become trapped, and not really know all the details of your situation ("where am I?" -- "your grave"), and sometimes that situation means you're simply in a position where you can't move, and die after you run out of auto-heals.
In any case, be forewarned, that if your skill level isn't high-enough, you hate practicing, or you don't like (or aren't good at) non-checkpoint/"save when they let you" games, this might not be the game for you.  Despite this, the game IS fun, looks good, and plays very well, which is why I will still mark it recommeded--but get it on sale, it's not worth full retail.

so, this is to be my first time reviewing a game on steam, and man, its a good one.
i hadn't played any RPGs before this one (unless you count the pokemon ranger games) and i went into it not knowing what to expect. fortunately, i noticed the free demo as i was about to click off and thought: "hey, what the heck, i'll give this a go."
from then on, as soon as it booted up the title screen, i was hooked. the combat feels really great and the dodging is just as offensive as it is defensive, allowing you to pull off range-melee-special (in that order) combos and do massive damage in seconds.
after i finished the demo (if you're unsure go play that) i immediately bought the full game, even though it isnt finished. i didn't care, the combat was so good, there is light bits of humour every now and then too, the characters were lovable, the story was better than i thought and i rarely play games for story (thats a lie, i own "to the moon"), and the world was awesome. now, the story goes (dont worry i aint spoiling anything) that you are a girl called lea who has been hacked into this mmo to try and get your memory back, now while it isnt an mmo, i remember myself constantly thinking: "if this was an mmo, i would play the heck out of it," because the world was really well designed. now as you travel through this world you meet new characters, the main side-character is called emilie and she accompanies you mostly throughout your journey in your party (yes there is a party system, i heard those are pretty common in RPGs), but whether she is or isnt available depends on if she's online, MORE WORLD BUILDING which is really cool cause it makes you feel like you're playing an actual MMO.
the sidequests are mostly pretty good and save you from grinding if you do them before you over level and the amount of exp you get from them becomes negligible. the dungeons are well designed and the bosses look and feel cool. especially the first one which is just the "hit the enemy crab in its weak spot for massive damage"
in conclusion, whether you're going in for the story, the characters, the awesome combat or just because the art style looks nice, i would highly recommend this game and even more so when it comes out of early-access. it has introduced me to the world of RPGs and you can be sure i'll be looking out for more in the future.

CrossCode is so far one of the top indie games of the last decade, and it hasn't even been released yet.
I've already put over 50 hours into this game.
I would rate it's difficulty overall as "very difficult," but absolutely fair, and I think that is a very accurate rating. The overall quality of this game is top-notch, with its attention to detail going above and beyond. The feel and pacing of the combat, the ingenuity required to solve some of its puzzles, and the ability to synthesize new techniques based off skills you've already learned in order to more overcome and solve new situations and obstacles. CrossCode does all of that, and nearly flawlessly.
This game is as puzzle-heavy as it is difficult with combat. Every nook and cranny in the game has some sort of adventure and treasure behind it. This makes the game's progression a bit predictable, but this kind of game style also isn't for everyone, as it can be "too" much in that direction for some players. I think CrossCode does this all really well though, and I was really really impressed playing the game.
The layout and aesthetic of each puzzle in CrossCode is top-notch, particularly the path-finding ones around Autumn's Rise and Bergen Trail. The colors, intricacies, and layout of each area take hold on your thoughts as you try and piece meal it all together. Almost all of CrossCode's secrets felt fair and worthwhile, and so I did them all without any real hints. Visually, later on, you'll encounter a really lush, dense environment that reminded me of the scene of stumbling across Tesla's 'castle' in The Prestige.
The music tracks are very relaxing, which was really nice. The game keeps a sobering pace with the appearance of 'tough' enemies: just as you think you've come out an area, something far more brutal to your life and your party's comes into your attention. The combat is varied and easy to get into, with different strategies required for almost every new enemy encounter. As well, Radical Fish Games has put a lot of effort into giving the player a really meaningfully clear and seamless transition to navigate, peruse, and switch out and use your gear and health items.
One thing I wish could have been explained a bit more was the saving system: The game saves whenever you change screens or visit a new area. This means that if you spend 20 minutes in one area killing baddies and searching that one piece of treasure, if you die, you lose all of it! But once you figure that out, saving becomes pretty quick.
To make this a perfect game for me I would want to see Radical Fish Games add in a little bit of a bigger splash of spontaneity into the game. There are a few areas where they have done something like this already (Pumpkin Funland???), but I want to see this spontaneousnes grab CrossCode by its horns and say "Hey! Don't forget about this!" Something to keep player thinking after they have already solved the game. But CrossCode isn't finishd yet; we have yet to see how the story and all its characters will play out.
The first time I accidentally aggro'd two friendly-looking enemies later in the game, they wiped my team and me in under 3 seconds. Those kinds of moments were some of the best, An enemy I initially hated grew to be one of my most liked after a particular encounter forced me to take them more seriously than I had before.
tl;dr it's as if Dark Souls took its combat and wrapped it in the clothes of Secret of Mana. 5 Stars, highly recommend.

Lords of War:
~~~~~~~~~~

The new Emperor calls on all the lords of Grandland to gather at the capital Canaanheim. Your father was the general and confidante of the previous emperor and was well respected by him. Now, nowhere to be found, and most likely fallen, it is in your blood to follow your father’s footsteps in Lords of War.
Lords of War is a strategy / cards game where you can play quests in single mode, as well as online PVP battles, and move up leagues as you successfully beat opponents.
At the start of the game, you’ll have to choose between one of several heroes. From here, you’ll be playing a so-called single player mode until you reach level five, where you‘ll unlock the multiplayer mode. The beauty of this game is that you can choose to play quests in the single player modes or face an online opponent in the multiplayer arena mode.
In my opinion, the single player mode is basically a tutorial until you reach level five. At the end of each of your battles, you will be awarded coins, experience points and new cards as you win battles. On some occasions, you might even earn a chest, too, which you can open and receive an additional six cards. Bear in mind, you’ll start with a fairly substantial number of coins when you launch the game for the first time. Therefore, you’ll be able to head up to the shop to purchase additional chests for further chances to unlock new and exciting cards.
For your first few battles, you have a restricted number of cards to choose from. Alternately, you’ll be able to have a deck of thirty cards to go into battle with. The great news is that as you successfully complete quests, you’ll gather more and more cards. Don’t panic, you’ll be able to create several decks of thirty cards as you go along.
The battles are fairly simple and well done. Whether you play in single mode or against an online opponent, each of you will start at the opposite side of the screen. The goal is to destroy your opponent’s base crystal to win the battle. Now, every nine seconds your crystal will generate one crystal point and the maximum it can gather is nine points. Your deck cards, or units if you prefer, have specific crystal points to be activated. Be careful how you use your card; even though they are drawn at random at the start of the battle, some can only be used once, so make sure you use them at the right time. That can become quite challenging at times. There are only four races to choose from. At first, you’ll play the human and will unlock the others as you progress throughout the game and reach new levels, which makes the game more exciting, too.
I must admit that the English grammar could have been better throughout the adventure mode. I rolled my eyes a few times here and there.
Graphically the game looks pretty good as its stand right now. And, bear in mind it is still on early access.  The music and sound effects are good, too, and the controls are pretty easy to use, as you would expect for this genre of game.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Nice graphics
-	Adventure mode (Single player) and PVP Mode
-	Stacks of cards
-	Ability to save several decks of cards
-	Plenty of people online
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	English translation could be greatly improved
-	No achievements or trading cards
Lords of War (EA) is one of the Arena PVP’s to keep an eye out for, and plenty of people are playing online too.
7/10

Since I'm from the UK, as soon as I saw BAF up on the Steam store I knew I had to have it. I wasn't dissapointed. There's a certain joy when using your countries armed forces in a video game and there is a definite joy when it's in a game such as ARMA II.

However it's not all sunshine and rainbows, there's no BAF tanks. This means that late-game CTI as the British is gimped seeing as how the other forces can pump out tanks.
Overall, if you want to breathe some new life into ARMA II then you should get this. Trying out all the new veichles and guns is fun as well as playing the new scenarios. It's best to get this on sale, with the PMC and Czech Army DLC too.

DISCLAIMER: I recommend any version of this beautiful game other than the pc port.
Deadly Premonition might be the greatest game of all time. While this review shall be focusing on the abominable pc version, I'll say this about the game itself: the graphics might be terrible, the sound effects were probably pulled from a free sound website, and it doesn't make much sense storywise at several points. But if you believe that games are about being immersed in a truly unique world, if gaming is not about getting an arbitrary number of points but is about telling a story in an amazing way that makes you care for the characters you see, I'd highly recommend you get this game for PS3 or Xbox 360.
Now onto the pc port, it's garbage. The problems are so numerous I have to seperate them into multiple catagories.
Crashes: Crashed 4 times in about 3.5 hours...maybe I could get a fanmade fix, but it's NEVER the fans' job to make sure the game works.
Controls: Space bar is draw weapon and aim (You can only fire and reload if you are aiming) I got used to this, but my problem is, while you can rebind many of the controls, you can't rebind aim to something resonable (Such as right mouse button) Also, certain buttons on the controller won't work if you bind them, for instance, I wanted to put the lock on command to left trigger. After I bound it, it did not work. Same as when I tried to put shoot onto right trigger.
Framerate: First half hour runs at about 10-15 fps, it ran fine for about an hour, now runs at a steady 5 fps. Uninstalling and reinstalling did not work.
Driving controls: They work fine (If a bit wonky) with a keyboard. When you use a controller, the physics speeds up so the cars, which only go about 60 mps in the game, can easily hit 150 on the open road and it makes the steering hyper sensitive. I thought at first the car's physics might have been locked to the framerate on consoles, explaining why on pc the cars go faster, since the pc version has a higher framerate. But why does it only effect controller?
In conclusion, the pc port sucks

On a technical standpoint this game is one of the worst ports of all time.
You will need a lot of patience to get the game running and to actually play it. Through the steam discussion thread that the dev posted I managed to get the game as stable as it could ever be. It would still occasionally crash after long sessions but it could be solved by saving often and restarting the game every now and then.
If you cant be bothered fixing the game, buy it on the console or watch a playthrough on youtube. Skipping this game entirely would be a real shame since it has a cast of interesting and weird characters with some cheesy B-movie moments.
One of the best scenes is the opening scene that shows agent Morgan smoking, on the phone talking about tom and jerry's S&M relationship, reviewing the evidence on his laptop and even holding a bag of evidence in front of his face all while driving through a curvy forest road on a rainy night.
The absurdity of that moment was one of the things that hooked me.
Without going too much into the story, you play a FBI agent investigating a murder case in a small town. This is the best part of the game since you get to interrogate the weird and interesting townsfolk and the identity of the killer is something that will keep you guessing throughout the game.
The gameplay is nothing special, car controls are bad and so is the map but by the middle of the game I found myself knowing the full town layout.
Shooting has been improved for the director's cut giving the gun infinite ammo and having a button that centers on the enemy. Yeah it removes some of the horror survival aspect of the game but makes the game way easier and less frustrating since shooting was a weaker part of the game.
You will need to manage a hunger meter and keep your clothes clean, its pretty trivial and would only become a pain when you try to skip to to do side quests.
In conclusion and a TL:DR for some people: This game is a gem, very raw and unpolished and I hope you wont skip it just because of the bad reviews.

A rather short game but fun all the way down. It is as fascinating to watch as it is to play. The fantastic idea gives you the power of being the protective creator of a tribal group of people by modelling nature and landscapes. Even if the main action of piling up and excavating the level's territory may not sound spectacular, I already played it through several times. Not least this is due to the physics which grant sensible effects from all my godlike actions. You have the power over lava, earth and water with which you can shape the landscape in favour of the tribe. The goal is to create a save passage over the map to some ruins which grant access to the next scenario. In this sandbox nature is your persistent opponent. If you are not careful fire burns your village down or flood washes your people away.
A real downside of this game is the story. Actually there is no notable plot which could be called a storyline. Other than the campaign you can also play in custom empty map where you can build your own landscapes.
It has also to be stated, that the game requires UPlay since it is an Ubisoft game.
So it is a game that is different. Unfortunately it is not complete, neither by its extent nor by its plot. Nontheless, it reminded me as well of endless hours in the sandpit during childhood. Not least thanks to the still pretty graphics I recommend this terraforming god game.

Series has not lost its unique charm. Basically a hilarious FPS loot-fest before the days of microtransactions and pay-to-win shenanigans (#screwEAgames).
Pros:
+ A standard playthrough has robbed me of many hours of sleep, which is totally fine for fun gaming
+ Voice acting is always a hoot, especially when different characters respond to NPCs and quests in their own way.
+ No lootboxes or microtransactions, because everybody hates that s**t
Cons:
- The characters aren't really anything much to write home about. IMO Borderlands 2 introduced some hilarious characters (like Tiny Tina, Sir Hammerlock, and Mr Torgue). The Pre-Sequel's new characters just don't have that sort of presence.
- Side quests can send you back to places you've already been to a lot, rather than focused on the area you're in. Since fast travel is limited to the New-U stations, that means a lot of time is spent getting from point A to B and then back to A to turn in the quest/shoot more baddies.
- Moon gravity and limited O2 (game's main difference from BL2) has led me to death by platforming fails more times than I'd like to admit.
Even though Pre-Sequel falls short of BL2, it's still a fun experience. You won't regret investing some time into this game.

Resident Evil Revelations is a survival horror game that was initially presented to 3ds in early 2012 and later in May 2013, was released for Playstation 3, Xbox 360, Wii U and PC. The game was initially launched as a spin off, however after a while Capcom, developer and distributor, announced that Revelations saga became a sub franchise that takes place between the events of RE 4 and 5, however is with story and gameplay focused the longtime public that cherished the real survival horror, and the main franchise would be directed to the masses and what was SH became an action game. However over time the CAPCOM seems that began to lose the main franchise giving as an example RE6 which had three campaigns, each of which had a different gameplay, one of them had survival horror, in another action and another campaign balanced containing elements of the other two. Something that should be clear is that the games did not become bad, just left to please an audience to please
other.
To understand part of the story:
"... Portrays the events shortly after the creation of a group to combat terrorism Bioterrorism Security Assessment Alliance (BSAA). One year before the game events, the Federal Bioterrorism. Commission (FBC) sent Parker Luciani and Jessica Sherawat agents to keep the "floating city" of Terragrigia under control after the bioterrorist Il Veltro organization launched an attack against the city using genetically modified living organisms, known as organic biological weapons (BOW) in opposition to the development of solar energy Terragrigia. At present, head BSAA Clive R. O'Brian sends agent of the BSAA Jill Valentine and Parker to search the agent of the BSAA Chris Redfield and Jessica in her last known location, the Queen Zenobia Cruise in the Mediterranean Sea ... About Gameplay:
The drive is too slow with certain characters are running or not, almost no difference, as well as pre configuration of the mouse crosshairs too, but it can be modified in sensitivity as well as one or another basic configuration. Wasd are used to move, the space serves to turn around, the mouse can use knife and aim, and the aim the knife button turns shooting the gun. The numbers mean the type of weapon you use and not to change the size, eg grenade to smoke bomb.
 thus switching arms defined, may occur by mouse wheel and the letters "Q" and "E". G means throwing items such as grenades and smoke bombs. "Shift" is walking and F are various functions as well as finalizing the enemy finally the F's (F1, F2, F3 ...) have functions from commands to another character to inventory.
The amount of weapons is good, and each has its own properties, but there are perks that are placed in slots (depending on the gun, it may have or not and if it has there may be more than one). Nevertheless, sometimes it seems that the weapons are unbalanced because it has weapons that can kill with one shot and others that need more than 6 or 7 shots to kill in this case even if you get to have more than 50 bullets that does not mean exactly what is enough. The character is very fragile taking an average of three blows to die, but there are herbs that can cure life completely. Tips:
1- use the dodge when with a few bullets, so saving. By the time the enemy is attacking press "W" or "space".
2- try to use herbs only when the screen is outlined in red.
3- shoot the legs of the enemy with the gun, so he will fall down and crawl, and can get away, recharge or use that time to finish unhurried.
Things that caught my attention in particular:
- The game is divided into chapters, and each time it will continue to match, we can see what happened in the previous chapters to reach the time in question.
- The game makes you spend a lot of items and to try to prevent a possible critical situation, we must explore every room to try to ensure the maximum possible items. That makes you better enjoy every detail of the game and also guarantees you more playing time.
- Files are found during the phases, containing information that best cover the story and expands the knowledge about the same.
RER it is an attempt to get back the feeling of a true survival horror, although not even close to the first, the game can do very well. I believe that last feeling at the start of the game was extended by the game completely, he would have got his goal. Unfortunately shortly after the game back to make the same mistakes and becomes just another action game. But not wrong understand the game is amazing, as well as all other franchise, but the game always ends up leaving the feeling of missing something...

In general, I try not to review early acess games, as any complaints or issues may or may not be solved. But every so often, a game comes along that deserves an early review. CrossCode deserves just this. Despite being unfinished as of yet, this game stands out.
Cross code is a game that will not hold your hand. It will teach you the controls, but from then on, does not hold back ethier.
Despite having clear snes insprations, this game has an identity of it's own. Fights happen in real time and leave you to figure out how to solve them. It's not a "mash this button to win" kinda of deal. Knowing when to dodge, when to block and when to fire abilites is critical.
Where CrossCode stands out especially well for me is it's writing and presentation. Despite having some things that still need work, the "game world" feels vibrant, immersive and fairly well polished.
There are witty comments and asides on the nature of gaming in general hidden all throughout. Party members comment on what your doing in a non-intrusive, often character driven way. Even random NPC's in the game respond in a way that seems to imply they have their own lives.
Honestly, the characters in this game each appear to have a personality of their own, with great moments of well placed facial expressions or moments of mystery. This even extends to the char you play, named Lea. She is unable to speak much, but is far from your typical slient hero, coming off charming despite barely saying anything.
Now, being early access this game does have a few issues. Particularly there are some balance issues to overcome. Sometimes the puzzles or boss fights can be overly punishing, expecting you to do near perfect to achieve a goal, or having some obscere angle that is required to pass an area. Platforming in this game is a major factor, and while working well most of the time, can be frustrating.
There is no "jump button." Walk to an edge and you'll jump, weither you want to or not.. meaning if you are trying to line up your character, you might instead jump before your ready and have to repeat the whole thing. Upgrading gear isn't too straightforward ethier, meaning you'll be farming for an upgrade for awhile many times, or will come across bosses that can nearly one shot you.
Then too, at this time, it should be mentioned that being an unfinished game, the story line is NOT complete. Despite these frustrations though, the game overall feels rewarding and fun to play. The RTS elements mean each fight is engauging. Even trash mobs take some forethought, such as how many you can take on and who is doing what when.
Indeed, while there is some rough edges to the game, the care that has gone into it is appearent. The game tries a few things to give some variety to the standard "beat up this to win." For the most part, this is done sucessfully. Also, the devs are active with their game and their community, with proper reasons why something is going to be happen. They have clear goal in mind, but are also not beneath having some fun with the masses in the process.
I am glad I purchased this game and dispite it's early acess status, I do recommend it.

Crosscode.... where to begin...
I can count the amount of games I've really enjoyed from start to complete finish (or in this case, almost finished) on a single hand. This game has great potential. So far? It's been pretty good. Let's get into it!
Story: (?/10) Can't rate the story since it's not finished, but thus far (8/10)
You can't talk. You can't remember. You make funny 'ha-ha's' with your 'why?' (..Not gonna spoil that too much, but it made me laugh a bit). That's pretty much it. A story of self-discovery for the most part. Oh, right.. and you have a creepy blue avatar stalker senpai.
Gameplay: 8/10
What I played was good. Fast, responsive, tactical, impactive and hard (depending on the situation). My most memorable events in this game would be taking down Apollo without a single scratch, and taking on the 'lighthouse' when it was just a 100 monster room without healing items. Got all 100 in a single go, but it was a decent challenge.
When enemies out level you, you'll definitely feel it though. They hit like bricks. Barely take any damage, but there's a single great thing. The quests, and story itself. It feels like a good mix. There's your super serious quests, and the funny ones. Take the Legendary Bunny one as an example. It has a decent mix.
The monsters are rather interesting. From raging bulls (of doom!) to snowmen (of doom!). To the cute little bunnies, sorry bunnies but I needed those exp points.
Hope you like puzzles, because some of them require a bit of thinking.
Sounds: 7/10
The music is amazing, the sounds for the attacks, and various other things are great. The splash sound when you purposefully jump into the water. However, this was made only better by the most fabulous voice acting (during april fools, doesn't affect my score). The songs were catchy, though... maybe Lea should get her own unique them? I mean Apollo's got that thing going on. "Hi... Hi.... Hi... Bye...Hi.."
Graphics (?/?)
Sorry, while the game looks amazing, I do not rate games on graphics. To be frank though, I'm still waiting on a giant rat boss.
Overall (8.5/10)
This game has the potential to be something great. For the first time in a good long while. This is a game I don't want to have an end, and go on potentially forever. Of course, all great things must come to an end. This game, fortunately, will still have some surprises for me. Hopefully, the game will have quite a bit more story after collecting all the elements, but time will tell.
Now, the big question. Is it worth the twenty dollars in its current state? Quite frankly? Yes, it's worth every penny. Despite not being entirely done, even if it doesn't (you better >.<). You still get an amazing experience for the value.
As of 11/25/2017. Still definitely worth it.

When I first purchased Stellaris I was amazed. It was like everything I wanted in a 4x space game, but after you play for a while, the critical flaws quickly become apparent. This game is wonderful on the outside and a rotten, hollow corpse on the inside. Consider this, 1 YEAR after release and there is still yet no way to mass-build fleets. Oh, you have a 800 fleet cap? Guess what you get to individually click to build every single one. Why in the world isn't there an option to have fleet templates? It's god-awful and makes the game tedious for me. There is a great many other reasons for my dislike of this game and i'll list a few of them below.
Positives:
+A lot of different types of government
+Terraforming
+Different weapons for your ships
+Hive mind species
+genetic alteration
+slaves
Negatives:
-No quality of life updates a year after release
-combat hollow
-diplomacy hollow
-warfare with other empires is a chore
-feels very unfinished
And many more. I honestly doubt any of these problems will be fixed. Stuff like the templates might be, but a few other reviewers share my thoughts that some of the major problems in this game might be rooted too deep in the core of this game to be fixed at all. Plus, this being a paradox game you'll more than likely be paying for any fixes to this game anyway. Don't buy this game at this point. It is not worth $40 USD at all.

Do you like games with great dark stories, memorable characters and awesome quests. If yes, then it is a no-brainer that you will like this game big time. It is also heavily underrated, so this one is a hidden gem. While it has some cheap mistakes, this game still deserves your attention.
The STORY[10/10] is one of the best I've ever known and I red a lot, seen a lot of movies, so yeah it's quite something. There are two protagonists: Mors Westford, who is an honorable man in the Night Watch and a mounstruos beast in combat. He has a dark past, lives in a cold place; you could say he's iron made. Also, he's a skinchanger, being able to control his hound. The other one, Alester Sarwyck, a Red Priest who can manipulate fire, who comes back to claim his title and land as a lord, now being ready to face the world he fled from. The villian is the evil-cunning-great fighter type, whom you'll want to kill the moment you see. Every key character ends being involved in the Game of Thrones, so things get brutal and the happy ending... up for debate.There are many sidequests that enhance the story and reward you with cool items(and experience).
The GRAPHICS[6.8/10] look outdated, but maxed out looks nice, and the artstyle is attractive. The real problem is reusing models, which means sometimes you'll have triplets in a cutscene. The main characters and all the places are unique, though, so work and clever thinking was used in the design as well. Such a shame it doesn't use better technologies, would have been a lot better for a lot more people.
COMBAT[8.9/10] is made as tactical, but as you'll progress in unlocking stronger abilities, you'll synergize with the battlefied, emerging victorious, without much thinking. Finishers depend on the class and weapons used, and both differ greatly from what you have at your disposal. I enjoyed combat and class exclusive abilities that I have a reason to replay the game. The downer here is the difficulty, if you play on Lord you might be stressed a lot, and that can happen on Knight too. Best you choose the Squire, since there is no achievment affected by the difficulty.

[Spoiler-Free Review]
Anodyne is an exploration game which borrows heavily from classic 2D Zelda titles (especially Link's Awakening). The dialogue is introspective, the subject matter is mature (sometimes even disturbing). It's also one of the strangest games I've ever played.
Exploration is at the core of the game. If Anodyne was a protest piece against hand-holding in video games it would be considered a masterpiece. You aren't given a whole lot of instruction regarding where to go next. This feels liberating, for the most part, as you alone are free to decide your next course of action. It's also intimidating and frustrating though, as getting lost/stuck at some point through your playthrough is pretty much a given. It's not necessarily bad game design, it's a product of having too open a world and too linear a path to success (i.e. to get past this next section, the player will have needed to speak with this person to get this item). There aren't many indicators letting you know whether you fulfill the prerequirements for an area so there's a lot of trial and error involved. Be patient or look up a guide.
All areas have their own themes and every dungeon offers up new challenges. This isn't the stereotypical fire/ice/earth/water stages type of game, the locales are varied and interesting: ranging from hotels to small towns and highway construction sites.
The soundtrack is excellent and deserves to be praised as such. It reminds me of EARTHBOUND most noticably. The atmosphere is palpable; brooding, imaginative, mysterious. I wish there was a sound test option to be able to listen to the soundtrack from the main title screen.
Aside from having a penchant for getting lost, the only other issues I'd express concerns about are the graphics and the flimsy gamepad controls.
The graphics are muddy and crude, utilizing a palette usually reserved for NES/GBC titles. They don't get in the way of the gameplay, but if you aren't a fan of pixel/sprite based games, you won't be convinced otherwise by Anodyne.
Although the XBOX 360 Controller is supported, the controls for movement are mapped to the analog stick and are very loose. I'd like to say this is a matter of preference, but when you're down to one health bar and your character charges at an enemy with reckless abandon despite your best efforts to carefully evade said foes, it's an issue. Nothing can be more frustrating than losing due to struggles with controls. A simple option to control the character using the digital pad would remedy this issue but as it stands, it isn't an option. I ended up remapping my controls through the joytokey program and my enjoyment with the game increased immediately.
If you like exploration games and don't mind the graphics, pick this one up. It'll surprise you.
P.S.
Anodyne easily takes the title for strangest post-game I've ever experienced. It's beyond interesting.

I have completed a guide which is a streamlined version of this review and includes the final technical tweaks that I used to make it all the way through the game. Best of luck!
I noticed that running the game in any type of Compatibilty Mode would cause the frame-rate to steadily drop until the point of being unplayable.
To get past the latest crashes, I re-launched in Windowed mode, with
Compatibilty Mode and was able to get past each crash the next launch, while windowed.
♥♥♥♥ that though. I did the following steps, and the game ran at a steady 60 fps and didn't crash within a 5+ hour session, which wasn't possible before:
1. Took DP.exe out of any kind of Compatibility Mode. Ran it normally (Windows 10 being the OS I run).
2. Set DPLauncher.exe to "Run as Administrator".
3. Ran DPLauncher.exe, and using Task Manager, set the Affinity of the process to use
Cores 0-3. With a quad-core, hyperthreading processor, this will mimic a dual-core, which is the game's recommended requirement.
4. While in Task Manager, I also set the DPLauncher.exe process to "High" priority.
5. I started the game via the Launcher and verified that the settings I applied to DPLauncher.exe were passed along to DP.exe (they were).
6. I proceeded to play crash-free at 60 fps for over 5 hours straight, which as I said, was a night and day difference to my experience prior to these changes.
Now, the bad news is that if you opt for this route, you have to do steps 3 and 4 each time you launch the game. The good news is it's very quick and easy. I should add too that the first 3 steps below (from my original review), specifically unintalling the LAV filters, were still needed for me to initially get past the intro video. The above steps ^^ wouldn't have gotten me past the crash at the very beginning.

Uninstall LAV Filters and VLC Player (if applicable). Make Windows Media Player default. Install the game normally then apply DPfix and SweetFX, if for nothing else than graphical enhancements. Nevermind about Compatibility Mode and simply perform the 6 steps I just mentioned. Then, while in game
, purely based on principal. I really believe though, with the processor tweaks applied, that the game will run much more stably...dare I say, rock-solid?

I have watched over this game since release to see how it ran and how well it evolved over time. I have watched several videos about the game, read reviews, and looked over the description and prices of Stellaris as well. It seemed quite liked and supported, but my love for astronomy and space pulled me toward it even more. After I bought the game, learned how to play, and tested all the features it had to offer, I was pleased with my purchase. Many of the bad reviews that I read over talked mostly about Paradox raising its prices and personally disagreeing with general comments from the game director. Well, first, let's explain No Man's Sky. NMS is a game that focuses around space travel, exploring, and gathering resources. Not many features were put into it, especially ones that were promised by the NMS team, which never actually came on release. No Man's Sky is very disliked, mainly because it's high price for a game that should still be in early alpha. Stellaris, however, contained many features that allowed you to play your own space empire and discover different stars, planets, asteroids, and strange events  going on elsewhere. It forces you to start from the invention of FTL (Faster Than Light) travel, which gives you no choice but to research new technologies and further advance your civilizations. You get to discover other empires around you. Maybe you want to trade with them, make them your ally, or possibly even fight them. Strategy games like this will force you to expand in multiple areas, to ensure your victory in conquering most of the galaxy's planets, or even in exterminating all life in the galaxy. Stellaris is a fantastic game in its current state, expanding in its different areas, or adding completely game-changing features will turn this game into a masterpiece. I highly recommend buying this game.

Okay, so Stellaris is getting a bad rap as of late, for...well...understandable reasons. At the moment, yes, the game is still in design, as is the current trend of pc games nowadays: make a game as fast as possible, sell it, then bugfix and tweak as necessesary. However, that does not mean the game is bland or "unfun." Now mind you, it is a 4X game in realtime, so unless you are a fan of 4X, this might not be a game you want to pick up. You need to make a bit of your own fun. However, what is beautiful about this game is beautiful. The late game is a tad frustrating, but the midgame is all about expanding and punching other people via as big a fleet as you can manage.
However, what really shines in this game, as of right now, is the modding community. And I mean SHINES. It is not Skyrim levels of modding, but it is getting there. Don't like an aspect of the game? Look on the workshop. Seriously. You'll find a great alternative, from fleets limping away from battles to changing completely how ethics works to game-changing traits to completely overhauled ships...
Stellaris is a HIGHLY moddable game and modders and even randos like me are constantly tweaking how they like their game, and changes from person to person. Once you get into getting mods the game takes on levels a team of developers would take years to reach.
Lastly, I know at least one developer, Wiz, is actively looking on the forum for things players hate and making sure they are addressed. I am not saying it does not take a while. Not much has changed over the past year gameplay-wise, but they are at least keeping an ear to their fanbase.
Lastly, so far Stellaris is not taking the route of other paradox games of bloated dlc. SO FAR. I WILL CHANGE MY REVIEW DEPENDING ON THE FUTURE, PARADOX! The DLC policy on your other games IS NOT OKAY AND I WILL NOT SUPPORT IT NO MATTER HOW MUCH I WANT CRUSADER KINGS 2!

Now we know that this is currently an "Early Access" title and that I shouldn't give too much praise but nonetheless I'll praise it as much as I can even if it's an "Early Access" title. CrossCode is an retro-inspired game with a unique gameplay mechanic (throwing balls) and was created by Radical Fish Games.
Ok so the story is that you are a girl named Lea, an avatar from CrossCode which is both the name of the game and the name of the game they are playing (a game inside of a game). In the 1st chapter, skiping what I call is the prologue (because there isn't much to discuss about "Shizuka" and her brother "Satoshi" yet.) There is this avatar named Lea as she awoken to a mysterious room. There she met Sergey and Carla, both notices that she can't speak, the reason why is because there is a
(an elaborate reason to make her mostly mute) but she can respond via head shaking. In that same place she learned how to throw
or
(or basically just balls) and learned how to use the
or
(or basically just a ring blade.). After learning that and talked to a bunch of people, and solve room puzzles.
The story is engaging from the start but loses its pace later on down the line, though curious about Lea's past and why did she have amnesia it falls down shortly (expecting the dev's will make the later parts of the game be interesting as hell) . Not saying that it is not interesting more like it is kind of a slow paced story.
This is just my opinion but, this game is surprisingly fun.The "throwing ball" mechanic works here with a good physics system. The 5 elements (currently just 4, neutral, heat, cold and shock) have their own strengths and weaknesses like a normal RPG has. The 5 elements gives you buffs take heat for an example, it increases your cold resistance. These elements will give your "balls" and your melee weapon (obviously) said elements but there is a catch to using these elements. Use too much and you will have an "Elemental Overload" which basically is just a cool down of the element you are using. Your default element is "neutral". The melee combat feel nice and rewarding, though sometimes awkward because you have to point your mouse near Lea to use melee which is fine by me. There is an exploit in using the melee and I'll let you guys find that out for yourselves.
The most RPG like element is the circuits and leveling-up, you can collect CP (or Circuit Points) to unlock a skill or increase your attack, defense, etc. The circuits have 5 panels corresponding to each element. To collect these "CP's" you will need to level with each level up's you will get 1 CP, some skills are required 2 or 4 CP to unlock therefore it is recommend that you finish the side-quests in the game as well as the main mission, or grind your way to level up or just do all of what I have said in one swoop (which I did). 
Oh there is also guarding in this game, it works fine to say at least. It feels just a bit awkward from dashing to guarding while defending yourself from hordes of enemies from all directions. The jump in this game is auto so you need to place yourself
From start to end the graphics looks amazing, it stayed true to its 16-bit style while adding more "spice" to it with the help of current knowledge and skills of modern day technology. From Rookie Harbor to So'najiz Temple the game really feels alive from my perspective (immersion), because the detail of each "art" was detailed.
When I say detailed I really meant detailed, the expressions of Lea are truly remarkable, and a nice way to send her emotions to the players around CrossCode and us players in real life.
Do you like retro, calming, and hyperactive music? Well this soundtrack is for you. Each stage has its own unique music and it really fits in. Passing by an autumn themed world with calming music to take in the world, then only to switch into a battle sound music with an enemy fighting you. I really like the music because it adds up to the immersion of the world of CrossCode and some of the soundtrack can be used for other things in real life like reading a book.
Lea is one thing (after all she IS the main character) and the other main cast like Sergey and Emilie. Like Lea, when Emilie is on your party she reacts to new things that you are doing and what you see and Sergey helps you behind the scenes and is one of the main plot movers (he gives Lea new words to speak). Most of the time if you are going to do the side-quests you'll be dealing with the characters in CrossCode, Each has their own wants and needs, what I noticed is that what they say if they are the players in CrossCode and not the NPC's is that it reminded me when I am playing in an MMO, so there a bit of chucks and giggles here and then. Most of the people (or creature) I talked in CrossCode has been interesting even with the cliches.
Dev's here are giving their best to complete the game and I respect them for that. Though I am praising this game too much there are some flaws too (like the auto jumping even though I don't really have any problems with it I just want to feel like I'm controlling my jumps the way I wanted it to be) but those flaws don't stop me from having a fantastic time playing this game.
So in result I give this game a
Is it worth your money?
"Kinda" if what I had said here fits your taste then don't hesitate to buy it. Even if you're not sure there is a demo on steam and their official website
Hopefully more and more updates will come and we get to see the story more.

This game is a very fun retro RPG, and I've really enjoyed playing it. If you're a fan of Secrets of Grindea or the Secret of Mana series, you'll probably enjoy this game very much. However, most reviews cover the positive points of the game fairly well, so I'd like to focus on the negative aspects of the game in this review. There are two big things that I want to touch on: The environment unnecessarily being used as a puzzle, and enemies that make me wait.
The backdrops and enemies are well-made, the character designs are pleasant, attack animations are fun to watch. The main issue I have with the design of this game is that it can sometimes be difficult to navigate the 3D landscape with the 2D camera. Many of the puzzles/hidden areas of the game are reached by finding climbable areas and platforming across an area, but sometimes the geography isn't completely clear. More than once I found myself walking back and forth between areas trying to find a ledge I could jump on in order to jump across the level because there was a small ledge that I'd been missing that just looked like a cliff. Other times, I try to jump from one cliff to the next, only to find that that cliff is actually higher than the one that I'm on, it just
like it's on the same level.
Although I do enjoy the platforming aspect of CrossCode -- climbing around the map on different tiers of the environment is a cool way to segment areas and encounters -- this design often feels more like a puzzle that the game leans on rather than exploration. Finding paths to treasure or quests rarely feels organic. It's fine to have 'hidden' areas, or treasures that aren't
to access, but more often than not, a quest or progression quickly becomes frustrating, because I'm spending time backtracking through levels to try to find the ONE ledge that I need to climb in order to jump across the entire level.
The combat system is fun and compelling, the inclusion of twin-stick shooter aspects alongside the beat-em-up melee mechanics keeps things varied, while the 'circuit' system gives you a couple different special abilities to play with. The problem is that although the combat
is fun, the combat
often drags. As you progress into the game, you begin running into enemies that require a lot of waiting around. The first such enemy you run into is some kind of mole/gopher/groundhog that runs away if you close into melee range; that's easy enough, the game is teaching me that sometimes I need to use my ranged attack. I get it, that's cool.
But eventually, you start running into enemies that are armored. Your damage to these enemies is negligible at best, so you're often left waiting for them to use a certain attack in order to Break them, at which point you're allowed to do damage. A lot of these enemies are only armored on one side, so theoretically you should just be able to get behind them to do damage, but in practice, the way that the enemies lock onto you and track your movement, this is next to impossible until, as before, the enemies use a certain attack that leaves them dazed or facing a certain direction. I hate this. I hate waiting around for these stupid goats to shoot their stupid horns at stupid me so that I can kill them. I've got places to be, I don't have time to wait on these jerks. Maybe I'm dealing with armored enemies the wrong way, and there's a lesson I missed at some point, but right now, as much as I enjoy the Break system, I cannot stress how much I
waiting around to use it in order to be allowed to progress in a completely routine encounter.
Overall, CrossCode is a very fun throwback to the golden age of RPGs. I'd like for the story to be revealed a
faster; I'm 15 hours in and I still have no idea why I'm
or how the introduction scene ties in to everything. I don't have an easy solution for the level design, because that's just kind of how the game is made at this point. For the combat, I'd like to see either a built-in counter system (one that doesn't require me to accrue SP to unlock it at the cost of something else) or some other mechanic that allows me to bypass armor, even if it's just temporarily -- some sort of default skill-based mechanic that can be used as an alternative to waiting to use the built-in Break system.
On a positive note, I do want to mention the text editor feature. I
the fact that the developers have built a tool into their Early Access game that allows me to provide direct feedback to them regarding the game's dialogue. Sometimes it's a little confusing (is this written wrong or does this NPC have a dialect or speech quirk?), but as a grammar freak, I
appreciate this tool, and I wish it was included in more games.
Overall, great game, I highly recommend it.

I didn't play this game until 2014, almost an entire decade since it was initially released, but it's still one of my favorite gaming experiences in a long time, which was kind of surprising as when I first began my journey into 'GUN' I thought I'd play for maybe three or four hours tops. I mean, nothing about this game looks special at all. The graphics are dated, the voice acting isn't great, and it looks rather generic by today's standards in almost every way possible.
It's safe to say that when I first picked this game up on sale, that I didn't expect more than 'Grand Theft Auto' on horseback. In fact, the biggest appeal of this game to me was the chance to do some good ole fashioned horseback riding; something I hadn't done since 'Ocarina of Time'. I never thought that I'd be so swept up into the dirty world of the wild wild west and the stories it had to tell me, but I was. From saving harlots, to chasing gangs down on horseback, to killing entire tribes of Indians in one fell swoop, this game includes every cliche you could possibly think about the wild west and I ain't complaining.
Aside from the tight controls, camera angels, and helpless harlots though, this game is just down right fun. And even though it's hard not to compare it to 'Grand Theft Auto' I never found myself thinking I was playing some cheap clone just in a different setting. And did I mention there were harlots?

For me this is one of my favorite games of all time and the best game set in the wild west. I know there are other, like Call of Juarez, but Gun, which is older, have far more interesting characters, world, story and I can safely say it's higher quality product, as far as the first Juarez. While the consoles have Red Dead Redemption, which by the looks of it is superior, PC have Gun, which is rough around the edges. I read somewhere, before RDR, Gun was the best western game. It may be rough, but this doesn't mean it's not fun. Unfortunately, it's far from perfect. It does have some problems, that might put off some people. It all depends of your tolerance for something far from perfect. Let me continue with bad stuff, so I can end on a positive note.
This is a console port and it's obvious. It's not the worst, but this could be unacceptable for some. The game runs at 30 fps, which is not such big deal, I can close my eyes, but in some situation dips below that. It's an open world game, but it feels like it's divide by sectors and when you reach the border of some sector, the game need to load the surroundings and fps drops below 30. It's for e second, but it's annoying.
There are some weird bugs. Few examples: NPC is giving me task and you can see his neck,arms and legs are not attached to the torso. In one side quest you can see in the distance, the enemies are riding … the air, or the legs of a horse are not moving. These bugs are more funny, than game breaking. The graphics didn't aged very well. For the time they were decent.
Maybe the biggest problem is the presence of slight auto aim. Why is this in a PC game? It would be nice if I could turn it off. The answer is simple – console port. The developer of the game is Neversoft, which were famous with the Tony Hawk franchise, but for the port is responsible Beenox (known for the Spider-man games) and they didn't do good job. Here is the contradiction. Maybe the auto aim it's not a bad thing, since aiming with the mouse is not perfect, it's not that precise. I always compare 3rd person action games with Max Payne in this regard, because the aiming there is perfect for me and Gun is almost there.
There are other 2 small problems. The first is the AI – sometimes it's just stupid and second one is the enemy models. You will see the same characters over and over.
After all I said, maybe you are asking yourself is there any good things in the game? Yes, there is. Absolutely love the game. Almost 10 years later, you can see the higher quality of the game, starting with the voice acting. The main characters are voiced by famous hollywood actors, like Thomas Jane, Kriss Kristoffersen, Lance Henriksen, Brad Dourif, Ron Perlman, Tom Skerritt. Even the other voice actors are doing a great job.
As a hole the sound design is great. The weapons sound like they came out from old western movie, which contribute to the atmosphere of the game. The music is phenomenal. When a track hits, you feel like you are in great adventure. And it is great.
The studio hire hollywood screen writer and the outcome is pretty good story. You take the role of Colton White, who with his father, makes a living with hunting and selling the meat to a steamboat. The steamboat is attacked, because the bad guys are looking for something, that your father is hiding even from you. He dies, the boat is destroyed and from here starts your adventure. The story is great, but short, so don't rush with her.
So is there anything else to do? You have a lot of side quests, most of them consists of killing everything that moves. But there are others, like get a cattle back to the their pens, making deliveries, protect people from wolves. And of course there are wanted posters. With them you often have a choice between dead or alive, which respectively brings you less or more money. When you are given a choice to get someone alive, the thing you have to do is to shoot the horse, cut him once or twice with the knife and apprehend him. You don't need to kill his buddies. And what is the wild west without a game of poker. In the two towns there are tables to play. The AI is not that good, but here is not that important.
While walking around you can find gold, which you can dig. So the first thing you have to do when you see shopkeeper is to buy pickaxe. Other things you can buy from him are standard upgrades for your weapons, horse, but not for the bow. For him you have to visit an indian outside the towns. There are two shopkeepers in the game and they sell different upgrades.
From everything I said until now, I almost didn't touch the gameplay. It's good. If you put aside the auto aim, everything else is great. You have pretty standard arsenal of weapons – pistols, rifles, shotguns, sharpshooter, whiskey bomb, dynamite and bow. My favorite is the shotgun. At close range is irreplaceable. After almost each story mission you will be given new weapon, each with different stats. In saddlebag you can choose which one to equip. The ammo for everything is not endless and you can't buy it. You have to find boxes with them in specific places spread around the world. Only for the pistols are endless and for the rifle are most easy to find.
There is one more thing and it is Quickdraw. This is basically bullet time. With a press of a button, you slow down time and arrows appear to show you where the bad guys are. Then you pres left or right and start shooting without reloading. The feeling of killing 6-7 guys this way is awesome. When you slow down time, you can shoot arrows and dynamite, while there are in the air. Of course, you can move the crosshair with the mouse. In some cases it's very useful for more accurate shots. You can also go in first person view, for better shots with the rifle and bow. As far as the bosses, all I can say they are a lot of fun, especially the final one.
Here is one interesting fact. Activision merged Neversoft with developer Infinity Ward in May 2014. In August 2014 it was discovered that inside the latest DLC for Infinity Ward's game Call of Duty: Ghost there was an easter egg of a fake poster advertising Gun 2.
The game run absolutely fine on Windows 7, 64 bit. There is widescreen fix, but it stretching the HUD. When you type in 1 in HUD_PATCH inside gun_res.ini, it will fix the stretching, but the mini map will be almost in the middle of the screen.
Gun is forgotten and underrated game. It's worth buying right now, if you don't mind the port. But it's definitely have to be played by everyone, who loves open world games and western movies. Gun is like human – it has some shortcomings, but if you look close enough, you will see beautiful soul underneath. From here you have to decide if you want to overlook the flaws, for everything else or not.

Before reading this review, keep in mind Tripwire is not a AAA developer, so try not to place the graphics of this game in comparison with Battlefield 1.
tl;dr Yes, this game is fun, captures the guerilla warfare used by the VC and the fire support by the Americans.
Graphics 7/10
Running this game on my rx480, allows for High settings at 60fps 1080p, foilage looks good, gun and player models are detailed, buildings capture that rundown and destroyed look, but the floor textures in forest maps are quite bad. All in all looks really good for a $25 game.
Gameplay 8/10
Game is really tough without teamwork and a competent commander. This is not a game where solo work wins the war, staying with your squad, marking locations for barrages, building tunnels as VC, and staying alive as American squad leaders will always win you the game.
On to guns. Bipods for LMGs are wonky as hell, but still functions well once you get to it. Flamethrowers has a volumetric system for the flames, so clearing out buildings are quite easy (you can tell by the screams of the burning people). Sawn off shotguns are OP as hell. Beating Americans to death with a pickaxe is fun as well.
Content 5/10
This is where the game falls short. The lack of gun modification and a lackluster progression system makes the game hard to stick to. A lot of classes are restricted to a limited selection of weapons, such as the american grunt limited to M16 and battle rifles only. Progression system, there is only clothing unlocks for soldiers, and each milestone unlock takes a LONG time to unlock.
Overall 6.5/10
All in all a decent game to pass the time, gets stale pretty quickly.

When I first purchased Stellaris I was amazed. It was like everything I wanted in a 4x space game, but after you play for a while, the critical flaws quickly become apparent. This game is wonderful on the outside and a rotten, hollow corpse on the inside. Consider this, 1 YEAR after release and there is still yet no way to mass-build fleets. Oh, you have a 800 fleet cap? Guess what you get to individually click to build every single one. Why in the world isn't there an option to have fleet templates? It's god-awful and makes the game tedious for me. There is a great many other reasons for my dislike of this game and i'll list a few of them below.
Positives:
+A lot of different types of government
+Terraforming
+Different weapons for your ships
+Hive mind species
+genetic alteration
+slaves
Negatives:
-No quality of life updates a year after release
-combat hollow
-diplomacy hollow
-warfare with other empires is a chore
-feels very unfinished
And many more. I honestly doubt any of these problems will be fixed. Stuff like the templates might be, but a few other reviewers share my thoughts that some of the major problems in this game might be rooted too deep in the core of this game to be fixed at all. Plus, this being a paradox game you'll more than likely be paying for any fixes to this game anyway. Don't buy this game at this point. It is not worth $40 USD at all.
